title: Width & Height: Controlling Size 📏
description: Set explicit dimensions, use min/max, and grasp auto vs percentage.

slides.title: The `width` and `height` Properties 📏
slides.content:
# Define the Content Area

- `width` – sets the width of the content area.
- `height` – sets the height.

Values can be:
- **Absolute:** `px`, `cm`, etc.
- **Relative:** `%` (of containing block), `vw`/`vh` (viewport), `em`/`rem`.
- **Keyword:** `auto` (default) – browser calculates based on content.

```css
div {
  width: 50%;  /* half the parent's width */
  height: 300px;
}
```
Note: `%` height only works if the parent has an explicit height.

quizData.question: `height: 100%;` always makes an element fill its parent's height.
quizData.explanation: The parent must have a defined height (not `auto`) for percentage height to work.

slides.title: Min and Max Constraints ⛓️
slides.content:
# Flexible Boundaries

- `min-width`, `max-width` – lower/upper bounds for width.
- `min-height`, `max-height` – same for height.

These are essential for responsive design:
```css
.container {
  width: 80%;
  max-width: 1200px;  /* never wider than 1200px */
  min-width: 320px;   /* never narrower than 320px */
}
```
The element will be 80% of its parent, but clamped between those values.

slides.title: Auto and Overflow 📦

quizData.question: What does `overflow: auto;` do?

options.text: Adds scrollbars only when the content overflows

quizData.explanation: `auto` shows scrollbars if needed, no scrollbar if content fits.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Avoid Fixed Heights When Possible

Setting a fixed `height` often leads to overflow or wasted space. Use `min-height` or let the content determine height for a more robust layout.
